According to the reporting requirements set out in the Regulation, by 30 April each year, Member States are obligated to publish and provide to the Commission detailed information regarding the application of the Regulation during the previous calendar year. This information must include several key elements:

(a) The plans for checks conducted and the risk criteria that formed the basis of these plans.

(b) The number and outcomes of checks performed on operators, non-SME traders, and other traders, presented in relation to the total number of such entities. This should also detail the types of non-compliance identified during these checks.

(c) The quantity of relevant products inspected compared to the total quantity of such products placed on the market or exported, including the countries of production. For products entering or leaving the market, quantities should be expressed in kilograms of net mass and, where applicable, in supplementary units as defined in Annex I to Regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 according to the relevant Harmonised System code. In other cases, quantities should be expressed in net mass, volume, or number of items. Supplementary units apply only when consistently defined for all subheadings under the relevant Harmonised System code referenced in the due diligence statement.

(d) Details of corrective actions taken in cases of non-compliance, in line with Article 24, as well as penalties imposed pursuant to Article 25.

(e) The percentage of checks conducted with prior warnings as per Article 16(13), with competent authorities required to justify the use of such warnings in their check reports.

Furthermore, by 30 October each year, the Commission services are required to publish a Union-wide overview summarizing the application of the Regulation. This overview is based on the data submitted by Member States under the above reporting obligations, providing a comprehensive picture of compliance and enforcement across the Union.

Article 28 of the Regulation mandates the development of an electronic interface by the Commission, aligned with the European Union Single Window Environment for Customs as established by Regulation (EU) 2022/2399. This interface is intended to facilitate the seamless transmission of data—particularly notifications and requests outlined in Article 26(6) to (9)—between national customs systems and the information system referenced in Article 33. The electronic interface must be operational by 30 June 2028.

Furthermore, the Commission is tasked with creating an electronic interface in line with Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2399 to support operators and traders in fulfilling their obligation to submit due diligence statements for relevant commodities or products, as required by Article 4 of this Regulation. This submission will be made through the national single window environment for customs, enabling traders to receive feedback from competent authorities. Additionally, the interface will allow the transmission of these due diligence statements to the information system mentioned in Article 33.

To ensure effective implementation, the Commission will adopt implementing acts detailing the arrangements for these electronic interfaces. These acts will specify the data to be transmitted, including formats, and establish procedures for the immediate and automatic notification of any changes in the status of due diligence statements by competent authorities to relevant customs authorities via the electronic interface. The implementing acts may also require that specific data from due diligence statements, essential for customs activities such as surveillance and fraud prevention, be transmitted and recorded in both Union and national customs systems. These acts will be adopted following the examination procedure set out in Article 36(2).

Operators are required to collect, organize, and retain comprehensive information, documents, and data demonstrating that relevant products comply with Article 3. This information must be kept for five years from the date the products are placed on the market or exported. For each relevant product, the operator must gather the following details, supported by evidence:

(a) A detailed description of the product, including its trade name and type. If the product contains or is made using wood, the common and full scientific names of the species must be included. The description should also list all relevant commodities or products contained in or used to make the product.

(b) The quantity of the product. For products entering or leaving the market, quantity should be expressed in kilograms of net mass and, where applicable, in the supplementary unit defined in Annex I to Council Regulation (EEC) No 2658/87, corresponding to the Harmonised System code. In other cases, quantity should be expressed in net mass, volume, or number of items, with supplementary units applied consistently across all subheadings under the relevant Harmonised System code.

(c) The country of production, including relevant parts thereof.

(d) The geolocation of all plots of land where the relevant commodities were produced, along with the date or time range of production. If the product contains commodities from multiple plots, geolocations for all must be provided. Any deforestation or forest degradation on these plots disqualifies the commodities and products from being marketed or exported. For products containing or made using cattle, or cattle fed with relevant products, geolocation must cover all establishments where the cattle were kept. For other products listed in Annex I, geolocation refers to the plots of land.

(e) The name, postal address, and email address of any business or person supplying the relevant products.

(f) The name, postal address, and email address of any business, operator, or trader to whom the products have been supplied.

(g) Adequately conclusive and verifiable information confirming that the products are deforestation-free.

(h) Adequately conclusive and verifiable information confirming that the relevant commodities were produced in compliance with the applicable legislation of the country of production, including any legal arrangements granting rights to use the land for production.

Furthermore, operators must make all collected information, documents, and data available to competent authorities upon request.
